items.q: What should you remember about **Three immune layers**?
items.a: **(1) physical barrier (skin + mucus-lined openings), (2) innate** rapid response (white blood cells, neutrophils, macrophages, NK cells, complement proteins), (3) adaptive slower targeted response (B/T cells, antibodies, memory).

items.q: What should you remember about **Mucus is a filter**?
items.a: **traps/kills pathogens; site-specific microbiomes (eyes,** mouth, nose, gut segments differ); nasal breathing filters better than mouth breathing.

items.q: What should you remember about **Fermented foods = mucosal defense**?
items.a: **2–4 low-sugar servings/day reduces** cytokine activity; fewer cells "calling for help.".

items.q: What should you remember about **Sickness behavior is motivated**?
items.a: **not laziness; vagus → hypothalamus → fever** (kills pathogens), photophobia (anterior thalamus → meninges), daytime sleep drive, lethargy, loss of grooming/appetite.

items.q: What should you remember about **Two sickness signaling speeds**?
items.a: **fast vagus pathway vs slow humoral** cytokines crossing choroid plexus → brain inflammation → poor cognition/memory when deeply ill.

items.q: What should you remember about **Glymphatic + foot elevation**?
items.a: **during early viral/bacterial infection, glymphatic** clearance ramps; ~12° heel elevation increases washout (pillows under feet).

items.q: What should you remember about **Cyclic hyperventilation protocol**?
items.a: **25–30 deep mouth breaths → exhale hold 15–60** s → 2–4 rounds; epinephrine drives anti-inflammatory IL-10; same stress system used for psychological and pathogen combat.

items.q: What should you remember about **Vacation sickness**?
items.a: **sustained adrenaline during crunch →** crash on rest → illness emerges; breathing tool mimics short-term immune boost.

items.q: What should you remember about **Hope = dopamine = immune**?
items.a: **sense of future activates** reward pathway; reduces inflammatory cytokines independent of "pure biology" framing.

items.q: What should you remember about **Spirulina for rhinitis**?
items.a: **2 g algae/day; 65–129 subject** RCTs; improved smell, sleep, work; reduced nasal itching/obstruction; alternative to Sudafed-class meds.
